# Brief

SpiderCaster's front door at spidercaster.com. Readers: developers and site
owners who want a site built from their own words, plus operators who will
run the builder on their own machines.

One page. A big hero that says the verb: write words, run a command, get a
site. Then the proof in order: how it goes in three moves, what you get,
the cost in plain numbers, old machines with the same job, the rules, the
check gate, the crew, install in two clicks, questions, and a closing panel.

Voice: human. Short sentences. Concrete nouns. No hype. Every number on the
page is a fact about the engine: 0-token drafts, 1-click install, 7 seats,
1 planning call, 14 frames, 0 failures allowed. No metrics, prices,
testimonials, or brand names. None exist in the sources, so none appear here.
This build stays noindex until a content gate is signed.

data.title: What you get
data.subhead: Everything on this list ships with the engine.

items.title: Offline drafts
items.body: one command builds a site from your words. The draft costs nothing and needs no keys.

items.title: Free help from models
items.body: the free chain can plan the shape of the site. Each try is written down with its token count.

items.title: Small edits
items.body: change one section at a time instead of rebuilding the whole site.

items.title: A strict checker
items.body: every page must pass every check with zero failures. One failure stops the job.

items.title: Plain files out
items.body: the site is ordinary HTML and CSS with the style baked in. No database, no login, no upkeep.

items.title: Room for seven seats
items.body: architect, content, frontend, graphics, visual critic, SEO, deployer. Each seat does its own job. None of them publish.

items.q: Does the offline draft really cost nothing?
items.a: Yes. No model runs. The words are sorted into sections by fixed rules, and the page is assembled from code. The ledger records the run at zero tokens.

items.q: What does the AI pass cost?
items.a: One planning call, with one retry if the answer comes back broken. On the free tier the cost is zero dollars. The ledger writes down the exact count either way.

items.q: Can the AI make things up?
items.a: No. It works only from the words in your files. It can reorder and shorten, but it cannot add facts, prices, or names.

items.q: How do I change one thing?
items.a: Edit the site.json file and rebuild from it with build --from. The rebuild costs nothing. Small fixes beat full rebuilds.

items.q: How does a site go live?
items.a: A person runs the bind command for the site and the mold. There is no publish button. A mold that is already live somewhere else is refused.

items.q: What do I need on my machine?
items.a: Python 3.11 or newer. That is all. The offline path needs no keys and no accounts.

items.title: Write the words
items.body: Say what the page is for and what it should say. A plain file is fine.

items.title: Build the draft
items.body: One command turns the words into a site, and the offline draft costs nothing.

items.title: Check the result
items.body: The checker reads every page and fails the job on the first problem. Nothing goes live with a failure on it.

data.title: Old machines, same job
data.subhead: Words in, pages out. That is the trade, and it is older than computers. A press from 1819. The ENIAC, wired by hand. Two women programming it in 1946. A room built to hold what people wrote.

data.title: The rules it runs on
data.subhead: Six rules. They hold unless Keith changes them.

items.title: Nothing invented
items.body: the builder only uses words it was given. A missing fact stays missing.

items.title: Hidden first
items.body: pages stay out of search results until a person signs off on the words.

items.title: Local photos only
items.body: a photo must sit in the project folder. Web addresses for photos are dropped.

items.title: Keys stay out
items.body: the engine reads key names from the environment. The values never touch the disk.

items.title: Every run counted
items.body: each attempt lands in a ledger with its token count, pass or fail.

items.title: Plain Python
items.body: version 3.11 or newer, standard library only, nothing to install.

data.title: The check gate
body: The checker reads every page before anything moves. Words against copy, links, photos, and the small print: title, description, noindex. One failure stops the job. Zero is the only passing score.

data.title: Seven seats, no publish
body: One site moves through seven seats in order: architect, content, frontend, graphics, visual critic, SEO, deployer. Each seat does its own job. The last seat writes a ticket. Going live is a person typing a command, and only Keith types that one.

data.title: Start with words.
data.body: Build a site like this. One page of writing is enough for a first draft. The draft costs nothing, and the files are yours to keep.
